newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Two killed in fresh sectarian attack in Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Two killed in fresh sectarian attack in Pakistan.

text.p: Gunmen killed two people, one of them a prominent Shi'ite Moslem activist, in the Pakistani town of Khanewal in Punjab province on Tuesday, police said.

They said Badr Abbas Shah, the president of the Khanewal branch of Tehrik-i-Jafria Pakistan (TJP), was shot dead by two attackers on a motorcyle as he was sitting on a bench outside a pharmacy in the city centre.
The owner of the pharmacy was also killed in the attack and a bystander was wounded.
There was no immediate claim of responsibility for the killing, which appeared to be the latest incident in a bloody feud between rival Sunni and Shi'ite Moslem militant groups.
At least two other Shi'ite leaders have been shot dead this year in Khanewal, about 50 km (31 miles) east of the central Punjab city of Multan.
A Shi'ite activist was killed on Monday and two of his companions were injured when a bomb they were carrying exploded near the northern Punjab town of Chakwal, police said.
